blocks.text:
Title:
Pressure Sensor Replacement (PS-04 → PS-04A) and Operating Pressure Update

Effective software revision 3.2, pressure sensor PS-04 is replaced by pressure sensor PS-04A at the HPU
discharge line. PS-04A uses an updated signal conditioning circuit and is not a form-fit-function replacement for
PS-04; controller firmware must be at revision 3.2 or later to read PS-04A correctly.

Alongside the sensor change, the normal HPU discharge pressure setpoint is revised from 180 bar to 200 bar.
This is a deliberate process change, not a sensor calibration artifact: the higher setpoint improves press cycle
time on Series-7 units manufactured after 2024.

PS-04 remains installed and supported on units running software revisions prior to 3.2. Do not install PS-04A on
a controller running firmware older than 3.2.

Field data showed PS-04's signal drift exceeded tolerance after approximately 18 months of continuous service
in high-cycle installations, occasionally triggering nuisance Alarm A19 (Sensor Signal Invalid). PS-04A corrects
this drift behavior.

Operator Manual AEG-OM-700, Maintenance Manual AEG-MM-700, and Component Register AEG-CR-700
have been updated to reflect PS-04A and the 200 bar setpoint. See also ECN-1058 for a related alarm
threshold correction.

Title:
Alarm A17 Threshold Reference Correction

The Alarm Reference (AEG-AL-700) description for Alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure Low) referenced the
pre-ECN-1042 pressure sensor (PS-04) by name. This notice corrects that reference: Alarm A17's low-pressure
condition is evaluated against whichever pressure sensor is active for the installed software revision (PS-04
prior to revision 3.2, PS-04A on revision 3.2 and later). The alarm's threshold logic itself is unchanged by this
notice.
This is a documentation correction only. No firmware or hardware change is required.
This notice does not change the operating pressure setpoint established in ECN-1042.

Aegis Series-7 HCS
New Operator Orientation — Hydraulic Power Unit Basics
Training Excerpt — Slides 4–6 of the full deck

What is the HPU?
The Hydraulic Power Unit is the heart of the press's hydraulic system.
You'll sometimes hear techs call it the "hydraulic pack" or just "the unit" — same thing.
It pulls fluid from the main reservoir and, on most Line 4/5 configurations, tops up from a smaller Auxiliary Reservoir during peak demand.
Discharge pressure is what the controller watches to decide if the unit is running normally.
Note: “Auxiliary Reservoir” is a Line 4/5-specific configuration detail and is not covered in the standard Operator Manual.

Before You Press Start
These four checks match the startup interlocks shown on the HOME screen of the HMI.
Full startup and shutdown procedures are in the Operator Manual (AEG-OM-700) — this slide is a quick memory aid only, not a replacement procedure.

blocks.text: Went out to look at the Line 4 HP unit again, still occasionally throwing the low pressure light even though it doesn't seem to actually be low. Talked to the shift lead, he said it's been doing this on and off since the sensor got swapped out.

Checked the gauge on the local panel and it read about 175 bar during a normal run, not 180 like the manual says it should be. Could be the gauge is a little off, didn't have a calibrated reference on me. Didn't check against the HMI diagnostics screen this time.
Valve (IV-21) looked fine, fully open, no leaks visible. Fluid level looked ok too, maybe a touch low but within the sight glass band.
Alarm history on the panel showed a couple of A17s over the last week, cleared themselves pretty quick each time based on what the operator said — didn't confirm the actual duration.

Recommend someone with a calibrated gauge go check the actual pressure properly, this was just a quick look. Also didn't get a chance to check what software revision the controller is running on this line, might be relevant.
— J. Torres, field service (no date recorded on original notebook page)

blocks.text:
Aegis Series-7 HCS — Maintenance Manual
AEG-MM-700 Rev 3

This manual covers scheduled maintenance, alarm response, and controller behavior for the Aegis Series-7
Hydraulic Control System (HCS). It supplements, and does not replace, the Operator Manual (AEG-OM-700).

Do NOT reset the PLC-03 controller while hydraulic pressure is above 50 bar. The controller reset routine
re-initializes valve driver outputs; if the circuit is still pressurized, this can produce a momentary uncommanded
actuation of Isolation Valve IV-21.

Controller reset is only permitted when pressure, as reported by the active pressure sensor (PS-04 on revisions
prior to 3.2, PS-04A on revision 3.2 and later), reads below 50 bar.

Alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure Low) may clear on its own within a few seconds if it was triggered by a transient
pressure dip during valve transition. If alarm A17 persists for more than 10 seconds, execute Shutdown
Procedure 4.7 before investigating further. Do not attempt to clear a persistent A17 by silencing the alarm
alone.

Shutdown Procedure 4.7: close IV-21, confirm pressure decay, set POWER selector to OFF, tag out per site
lockout/tagout procedure, then proceed to Section 6 (Troubleshooting).

If the HPU fails to reach normal operating pressure, check the following in order:
•
Isolation valve IV-21 is closed or partially closed.
•
Hydraulic fluid level is low.
•
Pressure sensor (PS-04 / PS-04A) signal is invalid or out of calibration — see Alarm A19 in the Alarm
Reference.

The Hydraulic Power Pack (HPU) maintenance access panel is secured by four quarter-turn fasteners. Remove
the panel only after the unit has been shut down per Section 4 and pressure has been bled per Section 8. Do
not operate the unit with the panel removed.

Engineering Change Notice ECN-1042 (pressure sensor replacement and setpoint change), ECN-1058 (alarm
threshold correction), and the Component Register (AEG-CR-700) should be consulted alongside this manual,
as component identifiers and setpoints have changed across software revisions.

1. Scope
This manual covers scheduled maintenance, alarm response, and controller behavior for the Aegis Series-7
Hydraulic Control System (HCS). It supplements, and does not replace, the Operator Manual (AEG-OM-700).
3. Controller Reset Conditions
Do NOT reset the PLC-03 controller while hydraulic pressure is above 50 bar. The controller reset routine
re-initializes valve driver outputs; if the circuit is still pressurized, this can produce a momentary uncommanded
actuation of Isolation Valve IV-21.
Controller reset is only permitted when pressure, as reported by the active pressure sensor (PS-04 on revisions
prior to 3.2, PS-04A on revision 3.2 and later), reads below 50 bar.
4. Alarm A17 Response
Alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure Low) may clear on its own within a few seconds if it was triggered by a transient
pressure dip during valve transition. If alarm A17 persists for more than 10 seconds, execute Shutdown
Procedure 4.7 before investigating further. Do not attempt to clear a persistent A17 by silencing the alarm
alone.
Shutdown Procedure 4.7: close IV-21, confirm pressure decay, set POWER selector to OFF, tag out per site
lockout/tagout procedure, then proceed to Section 6 (Troubleshooting).
6. Troubleshooting: Low Discharge Pressure
If the HPU fails to reach normal operating pressure, check the following in order:
•
Isolation valve IV-21 is closed or partially closed.
•
Hydraulic fluid level is low.
•
Pressure sensor (PS-04 / PS-04A) signal is invalid or out of calibration — see Alarm A19 in the Alarm
Reference.
7. Component Access
The Hydraulic Power Pack (HPU) maintenance access panel is secured by four quarter-turn fasteners. Remove
the panel only after the unit has been shut down per Section 4 and pressure has been bled per Section 8. Do
not operate the unit with the panel removed.
9. Related Documents
Engineering Change Notice ECN-1042 (pressure sensor replacement and setpoint change), ECN-1058 (alarm
threshold correction), and the Component Register (AEG-CR-700) should be consulted alongside this manual,
as component identifiers and setpoints have changed across software revisions.

AEG-OM-700 Rev 4
Document AEG-OM-700   |   Revision 4   |   Applies to software revision 3.2 and later

The Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Control System (HCS) provides closed-loop hydraulic pressure regulation for
industrial press lines. The system is built around the Hydraulic Power Unit (HPU), which supplies pressurized
fluid to the press circuit under the supervision of the HCS Controller (PLC-03).

Throughout Aegis documentation the Hydraulic Power Unit may also be referred to as the Hydraulic Unit or
the HP unit, depending on which department produced the document. All three terms refer to the same
physical assembly.

HPU
Hydraulic Power Unit
Generates and regulates hydraulic pressure

IV-21
Isolation Valve 21
Isolates the HPU from the press circuit

PS-04A
Pressure Sensor 04A
Reports HPU discharge pressure to PLC-03

PLC-03
HCS Controller
Supervises startup, monitoring, and alarms

Note: earlier Aegis units shipped with pressure sensor PS-04. As of software revision 3.2, PS-04 is superseded by PS-04A; see
Engineering Change Notice ECN-1042 for details.

Before starting, verify:
•
Hydraulic fluid level is within the normal band on the sight glass.
•
Isolation valve IV-21 is OPEN.
•
The emergency stop circuit is RESET.

WARNING: Do not start the Hydraulic Power Unit with the maintenance access panel removed. Rotating
components inside the HPU housing are exposed when the panel is off.

Startup sequence:
1
Turn the POWER selector to ON.
2
Press START.
3
Verify discharge pressure, as reported by PS-04A, reaches 200 bar. This is the normal operating pressure
for software revision 3.2 and later; see ECN-1042 for the pressure change history.

Normal HPU discharge pressure is 200 bar on software revision 3.2 and later. On revisions prior to 3.2, normal
discharge pressure was 180 bar, measured by the original PS-04 sensor. Do not compare live readings against

Aegis Series-7 HCS — Operator Manual

the 180 bar figure on a unit running revision 3.2 or later — the setpoint changed along with the sensor
replacement.

See the Aegis Alarm Reference (AEG-AL-700) for the full alarm list, including alarm A17 (Hydraulic Pressure
Low), its possible causes, and required operator actions.

Do not reset the PLC-03 controller while hydraulic pressure is above 50 bar. Resetting the controller under
pressure can cause an uncommanded valve transition. Bleed pressure below 50 bar first, using the manual
bleed procedure in Section 8, before performing a controller reset.

Product Name: Aegis HydroFluid-32. Recommended Use: hydraulic fluid for Aegis Series-7 Hydraulic Power
Units and compatible industrial hydraulic systems. Not for use as a brake fluid or in food-grade applications.

Classification: Not classified as hazardous under GHS for acute toxicity. May cause mild skin irritation with
prolonged contact. Slip hazard if spilled on hard flooring.

Base oil (petroleum, highly refined), 80-95%. Proprietary anti-wear and anti-oxidant additive package, 5-15%.
Exact composition withheld as a trade secret.

Skin contact: wash with soap and water. Eye contact: flush with water for 15 minutes. Ingestion: do not induce
vomiting; seek medical attention.

Suitable extinguishing media: CO2, dry chemical, foam. Flash point (Cleveland Open Cup): approximately
210°C.
Contain spill, absorb with inert material, dispose per local regulations. Avoid release to waterways.
Store in a cool, dry, well-ventilated area away from oxidizing agents. Keep container closed when not in use.
Use in well-ventilated areas. Nitrile gloves and safety glasses recommended for extended handling.
Appearance: clear amber liquid. Viscosity: ISO VG 32. Pour point: -33°C.
Stable under normal conditions. Avoid contact with strong oxidizers.
Low acute toxicity via oral, dermal, and inhalation routes based on component data.
Not listed as a hazardous substance under applicable regional regulations at the time of publication.

This SDS covers the hydraulic fluid product only and does not describe the operation, maintenance, alarms, or
electronic control behavior of any equipment the fluid is used in. Refer to the relevant equipment manufacturer's
documentation for equipment operating procedures.

Low acute toxicity via oral, dermal, and inhalation routes based on component data.
15. Regulatory Information
Not listed as a hazardous substance under applicable regional regulations at the time of publication.
16. Other Information
This SDS covers the hydraulic fluid product only and does not describe the operation, maintenance, alarms, or
electronic control behavior of any equipment the fluid is used in. Refer to the relevant equipment manufacturer's
documentation for equipment operating procedures.

This glossary lists officially defined terms used across Aegis Series-7 documentation. It is maintained separately from individual manuals and is not guaranteed to be updated at the same time as new Engineering Change Notices. Terms not listed here may still appear in other documents — absence from this glossary does not mean a term is invalid.

Note: this revision of the glossary does not yet include an entry for “HP unit” (used informally in the Operator Manual and training materials) or for the superseded sensor “PS-04”. Readers should not assume a term's absence here means it refers to something different from a listed term — cross-check against the Component Register.
Glossary Term: 'Hydraulic Power Unit (HPU)' = The assembly that generates and regulates hydraulic pressure for the press circuit. See also: Hydraulic Unit.
Glossary Term: 'Hydraulic Unit' = Informal short form of Hydraulic Power Unit, used interchangeably in some maintenance documentation.
Glossary Term: 'Isolation Valve (IV-21)' = The valve isolating the HPU from the downstream press circuit. Must be open before HPU startup.
Glossary Term: 'PLC-03' = The HCS Controller; supervises startup sequencing, alarm evaluation, and interlocks.
Glossary Term: 'Pressure Sensor 04A (PS-04A)' = The HPU discharge pressure transducer used on software revision 3.2 and later.
Glossary Term: 'Alarm' = A system-generated notification indicating an out-of-tolerance or fault condition. See the Alarm Reference for the current alarm list.
Glossary Term: 'Setpoint' = A configured target value (e.g. normal operating pressure) against which a live measurement is compared.
Glossary Term: 'Engineering Change Notice (ECN)' = A controlled document describing an approved change to equipment, software, or documentation.
Glossary Term: 'Software Revision' = The version identifier for HCS controller firmware, e.g. 3.2. Governs which components and setpoints are applicable.
